Use cases

Twelve business questions, twelve answers in social data.

Four families of questions: what your campaigns actually changed, what the market says about you, who your audiences really are, and what to build next. For each one we read what people post, search and ask AI, and a consultant tells you what it means.

  • Communication

Trusted by 50+ organisations · 160+ projects since 2022

Four families of questions

  1. 01 · Communication

    Make every campaign, event and spokesperson measurable.

    You already know what you published. The real question is what it moved: in which audiences, on which platforms, and whether the voices carrying it were the right ones. The online conversation answers all three, provided you read it beyond the volumes.

    The whole Communication family →
    • Analyze the impact of an event or campaignWhat a launch, a sponsorship or a keynote actually shifted: volume, reach, tone, and which audiences changed their position.→
    • Optimize your leader advocacy strategyHow your executives are heard next to their peers, on which subjects their voice earns attention, and where it adds noise.→
    • Identify the right ambassadorsFind the creators and public voices whose audience genuinely overlaps yours, not the ones with the largest follower count.→

  2. 02 · Brand health

    Know what the market says about you, before it becomes a problem.

    Brand health is not a quarterly survey. It is a continuous signal, already public: what your customers say about you, the words they repeat, the subjects that attach to your name. The work is to read it in time, and to tell the noise from what matters.

    The whole Brand health family →
    • Monitor your brand image and reputationTrack image, sentiment and the subjects attached to your name, continuously and across markets, with 24/7 alerting on the breaks.→
    • Develop your brand messagingSee which words, claims and proofs your audiences actually repeat, and which ones never leave your presentations.→
    • Identify and mitigate brand risksCatch weak signals early, while they are still containable: a rumour, a boycott call, a supplier controversy. Alerts within 15 minutes.→

  3. 03 · Audiences

    Replace the persona workshop with observed behaviour.

    Declared preferences and actual behaviour rarely match. The panel shows what people do, follow, buy and say when no one is asking them a question: a panel of about three billion consumers, read by analysts.

    The whole Audiences family →
    • Segment your target profilesProfile who actually buys, visits and talks about you: sociodemographics, interests, media diet, brand affinities. More than 5,000 criteria.→
    • Rejuvenate your audiencesUnderstand what the next generation of your category cares about, and how far that sits from your current base.→
    • Understand expectations at every touchpointMap what people expect before, during and after purchase, and where the experience breaks down, ranked by how often they surface.→

  4. 04 · Trends & innovation

    Decide what to build on evidence, not conviction.

    Every product decision is a bet on what people will want. The conversation of a market usually says it first: the needs nobody covers well, the irritants of existing products, the topics rising before they reach the surveys.

    The whole Trends & innovation family →
    • Test and evaluate your productsRead the unfiltered verdict on your products and your competitors': what gets praised, returned, or worked around.→
    • Analyze markets and identify opportunitiesSize the conversation of a market, spot the unmet needs and the whitespace nobody has claimed yet, before your competitors do.→
    • Map out your stakeholders and future trendsFollow the communities, experts and institutions that shape a category, and the trends breaking out of it before they go mainstream.→
